name: OOPS (Williams): gap beyond prior H/L, stop entry back at it, exit close
src: misc.invest.futures 1997 'Index Trading System!' (Badcock) + 2001 'Help with easy language': if open < low 1 bar ago buy at low+1 tick

name: OOPS held overnight (exit next open)
src: misc.invest.futures 1997: 'wait until the next day's open to exit ... profitability increased by as much as 50%'

name: Connors 10% OOPS: close in bottom/top 10% of range, gap beyond, stop entry at prior L/H
src: misc.invest.futures 1998 'Traders Electronic Magazine #4': close in bottom 10% of range and gap lower -> buy if it trades back above

name: Gap fade to prior close: open beyond prior close -> fade at open, target prior close, exit close
src: misc.invest.futures 1999 'How to Know an Open Probability': 85% of the time after any opening prices retrace to the previous close

name: Open +/- 0.29% breakout (Paragon), stop at open, exit close
src: misc.invest.futures 1998 Paragon Traders' Report: 'enter long if the S&Ps moved 3.30 points above the open'

name: Bull/Bear power stops from the open (Bear = H-C, Bull = C-L of yesterday), exit close
src: misc.invest.futures 1998: 'Let Bull Power = Close - Low; Bear Power = High - Close. Tomorrow after the open place a buy stop bear power up from the open'

name: SPI 'Grab'n'Run': buy every open, stop -1.1%, target +1.4%, exit close
src: misc.invest.futures 2000 'BUYING the SPI on the Open': StopLoss Open-34, Grab'n'Run Open+42 (SPI ~3050)

name: Buy every open, sell at +8 ticks (0.25%), else close
src: misc.invest.futures 2002 'Is it a good idea?': buy at the open every day and sell as soon as it hits 8 ticks

name: Early-session reversal: -0.4% under prior close in first 90 min -> 0.27% trailing buy stop; +0.4% -> 0.4% trailing sell stop; exit close
src: misc.invest.technical 1997: 'first 1 1/2 hours if the S&P trades -300 points from yesterday's close buy using a 200 point trailing buy stop' (S&P ~750)

name: Opening-range failure reversal: break of the 15-min range one way before 10:10, re-entry and break of the other side -> go with it, stop other side, exit close
src: misc.invest.futures 2000 'DAX Daytraders': within 20-40 mins the market reverses, re-enters the opening range, then penetrates beyond the range in the other direction, I go with that move

name: NR7 day -> next day buy/sell stop at prior H/L, stop other side, exit close
src: misc.invest.futures 1999 'T-Bond Day Trading': TODAY IS AN NR7 DAY, if YH is exceeded buy the breakout

name: NR4 day -> next day prior H/L breakout, exit close
src: misc.invest.futures 1999 'Day Trading Sep T-Bonds': NR4 SIGNAL, if YH is exceeded buy the breakout

name: Close in bottom 20% of the day's range -> long next day open->close (top 20% -> short)
src: misc.invest.futures 1999: 'a C<=20% Of The Day's Range signal working for us' (expects a higher close)

name: Gann pullback: uptrend (close > 200d SMA) + 3 lower lows (or 2 lower lows + inside day) -> buy stop above prior high, stop prior low, exit close
src: misc.invest.futures 1998 'What is a market turn?': Gann's pullback entry rule is 3 days of lower lows or 2 lower lows & an inside day; 1997: buy a breakout of the previous day's high IF in a larger uptrend after 3-4 lower lows

name: 5-day range 20% re-entry: close below 20% of the 5-day range then back above -> long (mirror short), stop-and-reverse
src: misc.invest.technical 1995: 'the old program I dug up on a BBS CD which buys when the close has gone below 20% of the range of the last five days' High-Low range then back above (and obverse for shorting)'

name: Hershey stochastic (5,2,3) enters 75% zone -> long, enters 25% -> short
src: misc.invest.futures 2002 'Jack: Please read': Enter long: Stochastic (5,2,3) enters the 75% Zone

name: Stochastic 5,2,2 fast line enters 80 -> long, exits 80 -> flat; enters/exits 20 short
src: misc.invest.futures 2002 'Question for Jack Hershey: Stochastics once again'

name: Stochastic 14,3: %K crosses up %D below 30 -> buy, crosses down above 70 -> sell
src: misc.invest.technical 1996: 'If SK<30 and SD<30 and SK<SD and SK next period > SD then buy'

name: Close vs upper/lower Bollinger (20,2): close above -> buy next open, below -> short
src: misc.invest.futures 1999: 'So if it closes above the upper band, we buy the next open'

name: Close above/below floor pivot (H+L+C)/3 -> long/short on the close
src: misc.invest.futures 1999: 'When it closes above the pivot, buy on the close ... below the pivot, sell on the close'

name: 40-day MA cross (long/short)
src: misc.invest.technical 1995: 'A buy signal would be generated if the share price ... crossed over the 40-day moving average'

name: 35-day MA: short below / long above
src: misc.invest.technical 1995: 'Sell and go short when close goes below 35 day ave'

name: 15-day MA closes (long/short)
src: misc.invest.technical 2001: 'a 15 Day moving average ... buy and sell on closes beyond that moving average'

name: 5/10-day MA cross (long/short)
src: misc.invest.futures 1998 'Characteristics of a Sound Trading Method': if our 5 day MA crosses over our 10 day MA we place a buy order

name: 8/20-day MA cross (long/short)
src: misc.invest.futures 1999 'Adaptive Trading': buy when the 8 day crosses above the 20 day

name: 200-day SMA long/flat
src: misc.invest.futures 2002: 'I buy when the stock exceeds its 200 day SMA ... sell when it closes below'

name: Channel breakout 89/13 (enter beyond 89-day extreme, exit beyond 13-day)
src: misc.invest.futures 1999 'Betsizing beats buy-and-hold': Channel Breakout entry 89 days, exit 13 days

name: Turtle 20-day breakout filtered by 20 vs 40-day MA
src: misc.invest.futures 1998 'Trading discussion': if the 20 day is below the 40 day look for 20 day breakouts on the short side

name: 21-day MA +/-3.5% band fade: close above +3.5% -> short until back at MA; below -3.5% -> long
src: misc.invest.futures 1998 'The Correction Is Coming': DJIA inside 3.5% of its 21DMA about 85% of the time

name: NDX down >= 3% on Monday -> buy close, sell Tuesday close
src: misc.invest.futures 2000: 'since 1983 when the NDX drops 3% or greater on a Monday the following Tuesday was an up day 69%'

name: Buy close of 2nd Friday of month, exit first profitable open (stop -1%)
src: misc.invest.futures 1999: 'Buy the S&P on the close of the second Friday of each month; $5,000 stop or exit on the first profitable opening'

name: Month/weekday seasonal: long Mon open->Fri close in Jan/Apr/Aug; short Thu close->Mon open in Feb/Jun/Jul/Oct/Nov
src: misc.invest.futures 1999: 'Buy on Mondays and sell on Fridays in January, April and August; Sell on Thursday and buy back Monday in February, June, July, October and November'

name: Weekend effect: long Monday open -> Monday close
src: misc.invest.futures 1999: 'people tend to sell stocks on friday close and buy them on monday open'

name: Seasonal: long Nov-Apr, flat May-Oct
src: misc.invest.futures 1998: 'entering the most bullish seasonal period for the stock market which has been profitable 80% of the time' (Oct/Nov)
